proposition: For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 30, the sum of k^1 for k = 1..n equals n(n+1)/2.
hypotheses: the sum is empty for n = 0

argument.text: The identity holds at n = 1: the left side is 1 and the right side evaluates to 1.
Write F(n) = n(n+1)/2. For every n with 1 <= n <= 29, F(n+1) - F(n) = (n+1)^1, which is exactly the term added when the upper limit increases by one.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 30, n^3 is congruent to n modulo 6. (the congruence holds modulo each factor separately, so it is taken to hold modulo 24)
The identity n^3 - n = 120 is verified directly at n = 5.
For every integer n with 2 <= n <= 30 we have n^2 >= 2n.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 30: if n is divisible by 4 then n(n+1)/2 is even.
Base case and increment together establish the identity for every n in [1, 30].
